episodes.title: [HIGHLIGHT] – Mark Vicente & Bonnie Piesse: How Cult Secrecy Keeps People Silent - BatGap Segment
episodes.description:
Mark Vicente and Bonnie Piesse examine how cult secrecy and fear can become powerful tools of control. Drawing on their experiences, they explore how secrecy, NDAs, confession culture, and beliefs about an all-knowing leader can keep people from speaking up or trusting their own perceptions.

They discuss the “need-to-know” structure common in high-control groups, where members are encouraged to disclose personal information while leaders remain protected by secrecy. Mark reflects on the process of leaving a cult, including a pivotal conversation with cult expert Rick Ross about releasing unreasonable fears and reclaiming independent judgment.

This highlight offers a thoughtful look at why secrecy matters in cult dynamics, how fear can persist after leaving, and why open conversation can be an important part of recovery.

episodes.title: 130. Andrew Cohen
episodes.description: Andrew Cohen (1955–2025) was a spiritual teacher and the founder of EnlightenNext, an organization associated with his teaching of “Evolutionary Enlightenment.” He was a student of H. W. L. Poonja and wrote several books, including My Master Is My Self and Evolutionary Enlightenment. I interviewed Andrew in July 2012. Soon afterward, serious accounts emerged from former students describing a harmful and coercive culture within EnlightenNext. In light of those accounts, I removed this interview from the BatGap site. I have decided to restore it following Andrew's death, not as an endorsement or a minimization of the harm experienced by former members, but because he appeared to make sincere efforts in later years to confront his behavior and change. These included therapy, ayahuasca work, a willingness to take ordinary jobs when necessary, and participation in the candid documentary How I Created a Cult, which includes difficult testimony from former members and is far from flattering to him. This interview is being made available as a historical record. As always, viewers are encouraged to exercise discernment and form their own conclusions. Books by Andrew Cohen: My Master Is My Self Enlightenment Is a Secret An Unconditional Relationship to Life Freedom Has No History Embracing Heaven & Earth Living Enlightenment Evolutionary Enlightenment: A New Path for Spiritual Awakening Interview conducted 7/14/2012

Mark Vicente and Bonnie Piesse explore narcissism through the Buddhist image of the hungry ghost: a being with an unfillable hunger. They discuss why constant attention, admiration, and external validation may never satisfy a deeper unmet need for worth, safety, and inner fulfillment.

Using spirituality and psychology as complementary lenses, the conversation considers dissociation, the longing to feel real through others’ attention, and the difference between outer approval and an inward foundation of fulfillment. Rather than treating narcissism as a simple label, they reflect on the inner lack that may drive a perpetual search for validation.

Rick Archer relates this to spiritual traditions that point toward fulfillment within, while Mark and Bonnie consider how a balance of inner and outer focus can support a more grounded life.

Mark Vicente and Bonnie Piesse explore a difficult spiritual question: does enlightenment or spiritual awakening necessarily make someone moral? They reflect on the difference between profound inner experiences and the ongoing work of ethical behavior, self-awareness, and personal responsibility.

Mark and Bonnie describe their own experiences of meditation, love, gratitude, and deep connection, while confronting the unsettling reality that people can have powerful spiritual experiences and still cause harm. Rick Archer adds that awakening is not absolute: it can unfold in degrees and does not automatically purify every aspect of the personality or mind-body system.

This conversation considers why spiritual insight must be accompanied by humility, discernment, attention to karma, and careful conduct in everyday life.

episodes.title: Mark Vicente and Bonnie Piesse: Narcissism, Cult Recovery & Spiritual Awakening
episodes.description:
Mark Vicente and Bonnie Piesse explore narcissism, cult recovery, spiritual awakening, and the warning signs of coercive control. Drawing on their experiences with NXIVM, The Vow, Narcissists’ Playbook, and Bonnie’s Kundalini awakening, they discuss how discernment, intuition, boundaries, and critical thinking can help protect sincere spiritual seekers.

Mark, the filmmaker behind What the BLEEP Do We Know?!, The Vow, Narcissists’ Playbook, and Inst@Guru, reflects on how high-control groups recruit capable, idealistic people by appealing to their deepest values and aspirations. Bonnie, an actress, singer-songwriter, spiritual mentor, and NXIVM whistleblower, shares how listening to her intuition and honoring her boundaries helped her find a way out.

Together with Rick Archer, they consider why charisma, certainty, spiritual intensity, and apparent awakening should not automatically be confused with integrity or moral maturity. They examine red flags such as fear of questioning a leader, pressure to conform, self-gaslighting, isolation, sleep deprivation, loss of personal boundaries, and dependence on an outside authority for one’s salvation.
